title: Library workshop planning
scenario: Library staff and volunteers plan an adult digital-skills workshop with capacity, access preferences, and an unresolved equipment question.
transcript:
[00:00] Leah: Welcome. We need to settle the shape of the adult digital-skills workshop before the library prints its monthly programme. We have a room reservation for Saturday afternoon, but the programme copy is still a draft. Today we can decide the session structure and identify anything that still needs checking.
[00:27] Omar: The small meeting room has twelve chairs around the tables. There is space for a clear route from the door to the back table if we do not add extra seating. I have not checked the larger room because another group is using it that afternoon.
[00:53] Nina: I would like to cap registration at ten participants. That leaves room for two facilitators without moving chairs into the route Omar mentioned. We can keep a waiting list, but I do not want the programme to imply that anyone on that list can arrive without a confirmed place.
[01:20] Caleb: Ten works for the exercise I prepared. It asks people to organise sample files into folders, then find a document using search. The sample documents are fictional. Nobody needs to sign into a personal account, and we should say that before people decide whether to register.
[01:46] Leah: Let us use ten places and a waiting list. A waiting-list entry is not a booking. Nina, please put that distinction in the confirmation message. The room reservation is from one until four, but that includes setup and cleanup; what teaching time are we proposing?
[02:11] Nina: I had written two until three thirty. My concern is ninety minutes of continuous instruction. Some participants may prefer a slower pace or a break. Could we teach for thirty minutes, pause for ten, and use the rest for practice and questions rather than another presentation?
[02:37] Caleb: Yes, though I would make the first explanation twenty minutes. People usually discover the useful questions when they try the task themselves. We could do an introduction, a short demonstration, practice, a break, and more practice. I can put that order on a one-page agenda.
[03:02] Omar: The break location matters too. The corridor gets busy when the children's programme ends. I can check whether the reading alcove is available, but I cannot reserve it myself. Until that is confirmed, we should not advertise a separate quiet room.
[03:25] Leah: Good distinction. We will include a ten-minute break and describe leaving and returning as optional. Omar will check the alcove with the desk supervisor by Tuesday. That is a request to investigate, not a promise that the space is available.
[03:48] Nina: For registration, I propose asking whether people want printed instructions, larger text, or a digital copy. We do not need to ask why. I can add an optional free-text field for other practical requests, but we should not imply that every request can be met without discussion.
[04:14] Caleb: Please include printed instructions as a normal option, not something people have to request as an exception. I can make one clear version with larger body text for everyone. For a digital copy, a plain document should work better than a scanned image of the handout.
[04:40] Leah: Agreed: a readable printed handout for each participant, plus an optional digital copy. Nina can collect practical requests without asking for personal explanations. If a request needs discussion, she will contact the person privately instead of adding that information to our shared planning notes.
[05:05] Omar: I checked the equipment cupboard this morning. We have eight working laptops and two that need updates. If both updates succeed, that reaches ten. If they do not, we would either need loan devices or paired practice, and those are different workshop experiences.
[05:29] Caleb: I would rather not make people share by default. Some may want time to repeat steps without another person waiting. Could we hold the registration announcement until we know about the two laptops? The programme printing deadline is Wednesday, so there is still a little time.
[05:55] Leah: We can keep the ten-person plan, but the final announcement depends on having ten usable devices. Omar, can you test the two updated laptops by Tuesday afternoon? If we are short, we will discuss capacity again. We are not deciding to reduce it today.
[06:20] Omar: Yes, Tuesday afternoon is possible. I will test opening the sample files, changing a folder name, and searching for a document. Merely reaching the sign-in screen would not tell us whether they work for the actual exercise. I will report the number that passes.
[06:45] Nina: Do we still want people to bring their own laptops? My draft says they can, but Caleb's instructions show one operating system. Supporting several systems may use most of our practice time, especially if a device has a different menu layout.
[07:08] Caleb: For this first session, I suggest using library laptops only. Participants can take the instructions home and ask general questions about another system, but we cannot promise device troubleshooting. That would keep the workshop description honest about what we are prepared to teach.
[07:32] Leah: Yes, use library laptops for this session. Remove the bring-your-own-device line. We can consider a separate troubleshooting event later, but there is no decision to run one. The title should be Organising files, rather than a broad promise to solve computer problems.
[07:56] Omar: I have a practical timing question. If teaching ends at three thirty, do we have until four to put the laptops away? The room calendar shows the next group arriving at four, and we need to leave the tables ready for them.
[08:20] Leah: Correct. Participant time is two until three thirty; setup starts at one and cleanup must finish by four. Please use the participant time in the public copy. The longer reservation belongs in the volunteer instructions so people do not arrive an hour early expecting teaching.
[08:45] Nina: I will revise the programme copy and confirmation message by Tuesday evening, after Omar's device report. I will mark them as drafts if the equipment question is still unresolved. I can also include the predictable session order once Caleb sends the agenda.
[09:09] Caleb: I will send the agenda and handout draft Monday afternoon. I will include the optional break, the sample-file exercise, and a short list of things the workshop does not cover. Please flag confusing words rather than just telling me the page feels too technical.
[09:34] Leah: We have a ten-person plan, library devices, a break, and printed instructions. Equipment readiness and the alcove remain open. Omar reports Tuesday, Caleb sends materials Monday, and Nina revises the copy Tuesday evening. No refreshments purchase was agreed today. Thanks; we can close there.
